$comment: The single source of truth for which Playwright spec runs where.
(the integrity gate) and the e2e jobs in .github/workflows/ci-web.yml.
Adding a spec file requires adding it to exactly one run here; a spec on disk that no
run claims fails the gate, and so does a spec named here that no longer exists.
A run's `env` holds the defaults for a local isolated stack; a variable already set in the
environment wins, which is how CI runs the same specs against its own ports.

gates.E2E_STACK: needs the isolated compose stack (scripts/e2e-stack.sh start --fresh)
gates.E2E_GAME: needs a running Veldrath.Server reachable at E2E_API_URL

stack-free.why: Pages and guards that need neither the API nor the database, so they run in the build job before any server exists.

stack.why: Journeys that drive a real server and a real Postgres: registration, the game loop, Foundry, staff surfaces, combat and layout.

outage.why: The spec stops the API to prove the pages say so, which takes the API away from anything sharing its run. One worker, on its own.

allowedSkips.contains: An earlier run emptied both authored chests
allowedSkips.reason: A stack that was not started with --fresh has already opened the two authored chests; the reopen window is minutes, not seconds, so the chest step cannot run again. The rest of the spec still runs.

The spec stops and restarts the API through scripts/e2e-stack.sh, which leaves a pid file this spec looks for. CI starts `dotnet run` itself against a service container, so there is no API for it to stop and it skips by design — the local stack run is where it executes.
